name: Telecom franchises and mobile-network retailers

problems.words: We miss monthly targets and only find out on the last two days
quick_ideas: Check progress against each target type every Monday, so you know by mid-month if you are behind
Split the monthly target into a weekly figure per outlet, so each manager has a number they can see.

workzap_build.text: A target tracker updated daily from staff entries showing progress by target type against days left, with a mid-month alert to the owner.

problems.ask_first: Which target is hardest to hit each month?
problems.free_stops: How targets are split and tracked per outlet is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each outlet's weekly sales with the same week last month, so slow branches show up before month end.
Give one person the job of writing each outlet's running total every evening, so shortfalls are spotted earlier.

problems.words: Operator incentives never match what we think we earned, and clawbacks hit SIMs we cannot see
quick_ideas: Keep your own monthly count of sales by incentive type, so there is a figure to check the operator's against
List every clawback with its month, so you see which periods and sales types it comes from.

workzap_build.text: An expected-versus-received incentive view with a clawback log by month and outlet.

problems.free_stops: Matching logic and clawback analysis are in the solution document; pi does not interpret operator policy.

extra_ideas.text: Note each disputed incentive line by sales month and outlet, so clawback patterns are easier to challenge with records.
Keep one notebook for all incentive disputes and updates, so old mismatches are not reopened from memory.

problems.words: SIM kits issued to BAs go missing or are not accounted for
quick_ideas: Sign every kit out and back in by serial number, so each one has a holder
Count each BA's kits at the end of every week, so gaps are found while they are small.

workzap_build.text: transfer_tracking — A serialised stock register for kits and handsets showing received, issued by role, sold and returned, with alerts for kits out too long.

problems.free_stops: Register structure and alert rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unassigned kit serials at each outlet this week, so you see where accountability is loosest.
Make one staff member hand over kits against a single written list each day, so missing stock has a last holder.

problems.words: Handsets sit for months while popular models are always out
quick_ideas: List every handset older than two months in stock, so slow stock is visible
Reorder by what sold last month, not by what the distributor offers.

workzap_build.text: nori_daily_read — A daily read of stock per outlet with ageing flags for slow handsets and low-stock alerts for fast ones.

problems.free_stops: Ageing and reorder logic are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk each outlet and note handsets untouched for the longest time, so slow movers are separated from genuine demand.
Give one person the weekly job of moving aged stock onto one shelf, so staff stop overlooking tied-up inventory.

problems.words: Moving stock between outlets is by phone and nobody records it
quick_ideas: Note every transfer on one shared list when it leaves, so it exists on record
Have the receiving outlet confirm the count on arrival, so gaps are caught at handover.

workzap_build.text: An inter-outlet transfer log with confirm-on-receipt that flags anything sent and not received.

problems.free_stops: Confirmation steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare stock sent and stock received on recent outlet transfers, so you see how often counts change in transit.
Use one transfer notebook that travels with the stock until handover, so both outlets refer to the same record.

problems.words: Field BAs claim sales but I cannot see what they did
quick_ideas: Ask each BA for a short daily note of places visited and sales made, so there is a record
Compare it with the activations the network company reports once a week, so claims and results meet.

workzap_build.text: A BA daily check-in and sales log by place name (not live tracking) rolled into a weekly view per BA.

problems.free_stops: Log design and comparison method are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many field claims name a place visited but no sale outcome, so weak activity reporting stands out.
Set one fixed time for field notes to reach one supervisor daily, so outside work stops arriving in fragments.

problems.words: Staff disagree about whose sale it was for incentive
quick_ideas: Write one sale-credit rule and share it with all staff, so disputes go back to the rule
Record the seller at the time of sale, not at month end.

workzap_build.text: A staff sales leaderboard with the agreed attribution rule applied to each sale.

problems.free_stops: How the rule is applied and shown is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which sale situations trigger the most credit arguments this month, so the rule can match real friction points.
Make the shift lead mark the credited seller at sale time in one place, so incentive ownership is settled early.

problems.words: Long queues for complaints and SIM replacements, and people leave angry
quick_ideas: Tally visitors by reason and hour for two weeks, so you see when complaints peak
Put a dedicated person on complaints at those hours, so sales customers are not stuck behind them.

workzap_build.text: A queue and visit-reason tally that feeds a staff roster for peak hours per outlet.

problems.free_stops: Tally categories and roster logic are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Tally how many complaint visitors leave before being served at busy hours, so the queue problem has a clear size.
Assign one staff member to own complaint handovers during peak times, so waiting customers are not restarted by each shift.

problems.words: Bad Google reviews about wait times are hurting our outlet
quick_ideas: Reply politely to each recent review, so readers see the outlet responds
Ask satisfied customers in person if they would leave an honest review, so the picture is fuller.

workzap_build.text: Automatic review requests to customers who agreed to be contacted after a smooth visit, with a weekly review summary per outlet.

problems.free_stops: Request timing and wording are in the solution document; reviews only ever come from real customers.

extra_ideas.text: Note the wait-time complaints mentioned most often in recent reviews, so the outlet sees the exact pain customers repeat.
Give one person the daily job of checking the walk-in line twice, so long waits are noticed before tempers rise.

problems.words: I run four outlets and see their numbers only when managers send screenshots
quick_ideas: Agree the same five figures every outlet sends each evening, so the numbers are comparable
Ask for them at a fixed time, so you are not chasing.

workzap_build.text: cash_reconciliation — A morning read of sales, stock and cash closing across every outlet, with the one outlet that needs attention.

problems.free_stops: Which figures and how they are collected is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note when each outlet's screenshot actually arrives for one week, so late reporting by branch is clear.
Make one manager collect all outlet figures into one notebook each evening, so you can review all branches together.

problems.words: Device returns and warranty cases are tracked on paper and lost
quick_ideas: Give every return a case number and one list, so nothing lives on loose paper
Note who has the device at each step, so customers get a straight answer.

workzap_build.text: A returns and warranty tracker with status and handover by role, reminding staff of cases waiting too long.

problems.free_stops: Case stages are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many return slips are missing the device location this week, so you see where warranty cases lose track.
Keep all return papers in one marked folder at the counter, so any staff member can find the case quickly.

never_say: Anything about tariffs, packages or operator policy.
Anything that helps issue SIMs without verification, re-use fingerprints or use another person's ID.
Anything that helps sell grey-market or non-registered handsets, or works around PTA, TDRA or CRTC rules.
Any request for customers' identity, numbers, biometric or account details.
Any view on operator contract or penalty disputes.

sample_reply.person: We keep realising on the 28th that we are behind on gross adds. Is there a fix for this?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there is, and you can start this week on your own. 1) Check progress against each target type every Monday, so you know by mid-month whether you are behind. 2) Turn the monthly target into a weekly number per outlet, so each manager can see their own gap. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a tracker fed by daily staff entries that shows progress against days left for every outlet and BA and alerts you mid-month. Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You are free to say no.
